Calculate normalised fluorescence from MST traces

Source: R/fnorm.R
mst_fnorm.Rd

Fnorm is the ratio of the mean fluorescence in a "hot" window, while the IR laser is on, to the mean fluorescence in a "cold" window just before it, expressed in per mille. Recalculating Fnorm from read_mst_traces() lets you choose the windows without going back to MO.Affinity Analysis.

Usage

mst_fnorm(data, hot, cold = c(-1, 0))

Arguments

data

A data frame of traces, as returned by read_mst_traces(), with columns time and fluorescence.

hot, cold

Start and end times of the hot and cold windows, in seconds, as numeric vectors of length 2. The hot window depends on how long the laser was on; look up the one used in MO.Affinity Analysis with read_mst_metadata().

Value

A tibble with one row per capillary, with the columns of data other than time, fluorescence and fluorescence_raw, plus response_type (always "fnorm") and response, the Fnorm in per mille. This is the same form as read_mst_dose_response(), ready for mst_fit().

Details

Windows include their start and exclude their end, as MO.Affinity Analysis does, so the results match its Fnorm for the same windows.

Examples

traces <- read_mst_traces(tidymst_example("dppr10-cy5_traces.xlsx"))
mst_fnorm(traces, hot = c(19, 20))
#> # A tibble: 80 × 16
#>    merge_set       run       capillary measured_at         capillary_type ligand

# Use a shorter hot window, excluding outliers
traces |>
  dplyr::filter(included) |>
  mst_fnorm(hot = c(1.5, 2.5))
